summary: EcoJukebox translates real-time environmental telemetry into dynamic audio via data sonification. Utilizing an ESP32 microcontroller, the system acquires localized microclimatic parameters—specifically soil moisture alongside ambient temperature and relative humidity—via an AHT20 sensor, cross-verified by a redundant DHT11 sensor. These readings are transmitted to a web interface (audio.php) to synthesize live acoustic feedback, mapping aridity and thermal intensity to musical tempo and pitch. Finally, local datasets are benchmarked against global NASA repositories (SMAP and GISS) to contextualize micro-environmental anomalies within planetary climate trends.
details: EcoJukebox translates real-time environmental data into live music via data sonification, allowing audiences to "hear" ecological shifts rather than just viewing static charts. Its hardware architecture relies on an ESP32 microcontroller that collects localized telemetry using a soil moisture sensor and an AHT20 air temperature and humidity sensor, cross-verified by a redundant DHT11 sensor for data reliability. This live sensor data is transmitted over Wi-Fi to a web interface (audio.php) that dynamically maps environmental thresholds to sound—where dry soil triggers fast, high-pitched alert tones, and damp soil and cooler temperatures generate calm, harmonic melodies. Additionally, local measurements are cross-referenced with NASA SMAP (global satellite soil moisture) and NASA GISS (historical global temperature records since 1880) to contextualize local microclimates within planetary trends, combining IoT, Earth science, and music into an accessible, low-cost STEM tool for environmental monitoring and inclusive science communication.
dataRefs: We integrate NASA satellite data into our local project to benchmark and contextualize our micro-environmental measurements.
